history.period: present marble complex 19th century CE (legend of the sati dated 1295 or 1595 - disputed)
history.summary: Major Marwari pilgrimage temple in Jhunjhunu, Shekhawati, dedicated to Narayani Devi (worshipped as Dadiji), the first of thirteen satis in the Jalan (Agarwal) lineage; legend identifies her as Uttara reborn (Mahabharata) and says the horse carrying her ashes stopped at Jhunjhunu, where the temple was built. There is no idol - a trishul is the main object of worship. The legend's date is disputed (1295 vs 1595 are both cited; the 400th anniversary was celebrated in 1996); the present white-marble complex was raised by the merchant community, one source dating it to the 19th century. OPENING-HOURS CONFLICT: the temple trust's site lists 4:00 AM-11:00 PM daily; a travel site lists 8 AM-12:30 PM, 3-5 PM, 6:30-9 PM. CSV TOWN CORRECTION: the actual town is Jhunjhunu, not Sikar.

name: Rani Sati Temple
town_description: Jhunjhunu, in the Shekhawati region of northern Rajasthan, is known as the 'open-air art gallery of Rajasthan' for its frescoed merchant havelis, and is the chief town of the district of the same name.

travel.road: Well connected by road to Jaipur, Bikaner and Delhi via NH-11 and state highways
